title: Mushroom
summary: A mushroom is the spore-making part of a fungus; the rest of the fungus is a hidden web of threads in the soil.

layers.basics: What you see is only the fruit. Underground the fungus is a network of fine threads that digests dead material and absorbs the nutrients. The cap makes dust-like spores that drift away to start new fungi. Zoom in to the underside of a cap.
layers.deeper: The threads are called hyphae and together they form a mycelium. Under a gilled cap, the thin plates called gills are lined with club-shaped cells (basidia) that each carry spores on tiny stalks.
layers.expert: Hyphae are tubes enclosed in a cell wall whose main structural polymer is typically chitin. Basidia typically bear four spores, which are shot off by a drop of water that condenses at the spore's base. The park is a simplified scene, not a scan of a real place.
